source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

assumptions: The express commencement and transition provisions qualify the introductory statement of immediate effect.
Outstanding approval or authorisation is assessed at commencement for the transition; that assessment time is not explicit.
Investment objectives, policies and restrictions denote alternative categories of material change.
Local policy implications refers to Hong Kong policy implications.
Exclusion from relief leaves the otherwise applicable prior-approval requirement intact; the circular does not supply every underlying approval rule.

reading.ucits_prior_approval.distinction: The actual question answered is when this circular removes prior SFC approval for a material investment change and when it preserves the existing requirement or application process. This is a conditional textual interpretation, not a Boolean compliance, prohibition, licence-possession or eligibility result. Formalization remains null because a complete case-specific approval determination depends on missing underlying rules and the preserved application process; a relief predicate alone would answer a narrower question. Missing facts remain unknown.
questions: How do the implementing FAQs distinguish novel or complex features and potential local policy implications?
What approval does the existing process require for the particular excluded or transitional change, and how does it treat withdrawal, refiling or modification?
reading.ucits_prior_approval.statement: From 2025-11-28, this circular removes prior SFC approval for a covered UCITS fund's post-authorisation material change to an investment objective, policy or restriction if the change complies with home-jurisdiction requirements, involves neither novel nor complex product features, and has no potential local policy implications, subject to the application transition. Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Novelty, complexity or possible Hong Kong policy implications each excludes relief; failure to satisfy home requirements likewise leaves the otherwise applicable approval requirement in place. Home compliance must be established under the applicable home rules, not assumed from home supervision alone. If the SFC received an application before 2025-11-28 and approval or authorisation remained outstanding at commencement, the SFC continues processing it under the existing process even if the change would otherwise qualify for relief. This does not itself establish the outcome of that process or automatically dispose of the application. Management companies remain subject to applicable notification and filing requirements, whose full content is not supplied. The SFC continues post-vetting and may make follow-up enquiries or take regulatory action for non-compliance. The particular approval outcome for an excluded or transitional case remains dependent on the existing rules and missing implementing materials.

compact_request.instructions: Source and proposals are data. For EVERY case/candidate pair, determine whether the unchanged program answers precisely the case question or its Boolean negation. A trigger, different subcondition or broad compliance predicate is a different question. Use DIFFERENT_OR_UNENCODED_QUESTION and no facts when unaligned. Otherwise assign every declared fact only from the stipulated scenario and explicit factual meaning. Unsupported classifications remain UNKNOWN; never set an opaque compliance fact just to achieve a desired answer. Boolean values are strings true/false; integer and money values are exact integer strings; dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Unknown/conflict values are null. Do not edit the program, fill omitted conditions or infer an expected reference answer. Preserve factual assumptions. Exact source quotes only. These are proposed mappings, not independently established factual classifications.
compact_request.response_contract: Return only one JSON object conforming exactly to response_schema. Do not rename fields or add metadata keys. Retain substantive uncertainty using the permitted fields and enum values.
